about.title: Personal Injury Help in San Anselmo, California
about.longDescription: San Anselmo is a small town, but its streets carry real traffic — and real risk. Public records show 29 injury collisions in the most recent final reporting year, leaving 36 people hurt. The corridors that see the most reported activity include Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Center Boulevard, Butterfield Road, and San Anselmo Avenue, streets locals use every day to get to work, school, or downtown. If you were injured in one of these incidents, you're probably dealing with more than just physical pain — missed work, medical bills, insurance calls, and a lot of uncertainty about what happens next. LawProactive is a free service that helps injured people in San Anselmo connect with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at what happened and explain your options. We are not a law firm, and we don't provide legal advice ourselves. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out costs nothing and doesn't commit you to anything — it's simply a way to get informed before decisions have to be made.

whyChoose.title: Why San Anselmo Residents Reach Out to Us

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California law generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Getting informed early helps protect that window.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Suffered
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so your claim isn't artificially limited by a fixed dollar ceiling.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless there's a recovery. That means getting legal guidance doesn't add financial pressure while you're already dealing with medical bills.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in San Anselmo?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity — like a city or county vehicle — was involved, the window can be much shorter, sometimes just six months. It's worth getting informed early rather than waiting.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means being partially at fault doesn't automatically bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of responsibility. An attorney can help assess how fault might be allocated in your situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in San Anselmo?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher reported activity along Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Center Boulevard, Butterfield Road, and San Anselmo Avenue, with Thursdays between 5 and 7 p.m. showing more frequent reports. These are simply neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. This is different from some other states, so it's worth discussing your specific situation with an attorney.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
